The 2027 Bavaria I740FC Unik Is a Class-A Motorhome With Plenty of Style and Substance
23 photos
Photo: YouTube/Campingcarlesite
Name your product Unik ("unique"), and it'd better deliver something that would set it apart from anything else on the market. The Bavaria I740FC Unik motorhome isn't unique for its layout or its finishes, but the way in which it combines both makes it a true standout.
The Bavaria I740FC Unik is just one of the motorhomes offered by French manufacturer Bavaria Camping, which currently operates under the Pilote Group umbrella . It's part of the Class-A series, so it's an integrated model design to carry and sleep four passengers, with an optional fifth bed available as an extra.
As noted already, what makes this model stand out isn't the layout, which is neither new for Bavaria nor never done by someone else, or the finishes. It's the combination of both and how they work together to deliver a motorhome that is equal parts style and substance: a nice, very elegant home on wheels that's just perfect for extended adventures.
Bavaria Camping describes it as "a vehicle you can rely on," which is a good starting point for an investment you plan on making the most of for years to come, in all types of scenarios. The model debuted for the 2024 model year but the 2027 iteration brings its most drastic refresh to date, or what the media called a modern new face for the modern interior.
Photo: YouTube/Campingcarlesite The base for the RV is the new Fiat Ducato CSS Euro 6E chassis, offered with a new, streamlined and more angular front end. Depending on who you ask, this front end either makes the RV look perpetually angry, but in a cute, Frenchie-like kind of way, or obnoxiously boxy. Bavaria chooses to believe that it adds a more modern, even futuristic appeal.
The same goes for parent company Pilote Groupe, which started showing the same front end on other models last summer. Other European manufacturers are also toying with this angular aesthetic, so it's definitely something in the air over here.
Aesthetics aside, which we can all agree will be perceived differently from person to person, the chassis brings a bit of extra length. It's not much – just 7 centimeters (2.7 inches) in overall length – but it's centimeters that you get, not lose, so you will have a bit more space inside.
Photo: YouTube/Campingcarlesite Since we're on the topic of overall length , it comes in at 7.56 meters (25 feet) for 2027. Width remains the same as in previous years, 2.3 meters (7.5 feet), with an overall height of 2.88 meters (9.4 feet). The motorhome comes standard with a 2.2-liter engine with 180 hp and an automatic transmission.
The interior remains more or less unchanged from the previous years, while the layout is fully unchanged. This is an RV designed for a four-person family, offering two separate sleeping areas, one of which will be fixed, a five-person dining space that can convert into a third sleeping area as an option, a standard but nicer looking galley kitchen, and a pass-through dry bathroom.
The highlight is the main bedroom at the rear, with a queen island bed on an elevated platform so you have ample walkaround space and room for storage in matching wardrobes, overhead cabinets, and his and hers nightstands. Bavaria keeps the cherry on the cake as an option, though: you get to choose a height-adjustable bed that, at a single press of a button, will go up and down, creating more headroom inside the pass-through garage underneath.
Photo: YouTube/Campingcarlesite That's the second highlight of the model. The oversize garage at the back is accessed from three sides, two on either side of the RV and from inside, and comes with tie-downs, additional shelving, lights, heat, an outside shower, and the optional adjustable height that will allow you to pack in there items like bicycles.
For 2027, the Bavaria I740FC comes with upgraded and plushier cushions in the living room, a new kitchen backsplash, and the same elegant wood cabinetry in neutral colors, with darker acoustic wall panels and black hardware for accent.
The dinette is also the lounge and it's spacious enough to fit five people comfortably . You get a face-to-face seating arrangement with two generous benches and a fold-out table, with the cabin seats swiveling to face the interior for even more seating. Over this space is the drop-down automatic bed, nicely integrated into the ceiling but large enough to be comfortable for two adults.
Photo: YouTube/Campingcarlesite The kitchen is standard for a European motorhome , which means you get a single-block unit with a separate tower fridge with freezer, a two-burner gas cooktop, a nice sink with cover, and plenty of storage. It's a good-looking and nicely appointed space that will help you get the job done, but without being too nit-picky about it.
The bathroom offers a large walk-in shower on the campside and the toilet room on the other side, with enough space in between so that, when you close the partition doors to the bedroom and kitchen space, you have a changing room. Alternatively, this split layout is ideal for traveling families, allowing two people to use the facilities at the same time. If you've ever been in a queue to the bathroom with an emergency, you know.
The Bavaria I740FC Unik comes with full insulation, a Combi D6E Truma heater and 6000W diesel-electric water heater, an Xperience digital command panel, and pre-wiring for solar and TV. Holding tanks hold 130 liters (34 gallons) of freshwater and 95 liters (25 gallons) of gray. Since the toilet is a cassette-style one, there is no black tank onboard.
Photo: YouTube/Campingcarlesite This motorhome has a maximum permissible weight of 3,500 kg (7,716 lbs) with 488 kg (1,076 lbs) of payload. That means that it can be operated on a standard B Category driving license without having to upgrade.
The 2027 model year starts at €87,900, which is roughly $95,900 at the current exchange rate.
